All — reviewed Triton_MSA_redline_v3.docx. High-level recommendations (legal):

1) Notice window: standard practice is 60–90 days depending on onboarding/transfer runbooks. Given we're offering dedicated capacity on this order form, 60 days is defensible. If Triton pushes to 45 we can accept for pilot-only customers or lower TCV deals.

2) Termination-for-convenience (TFC): we should preserve a TFC that covers reasonable wind-down costs. Suggested approach:
   - Enterprise order forms: TFC = greater of (3 months of average monthly revenue) or actual documented wind-down costs, with a 90-day cure/right-to-cure for service team to mitigate immediate exposure.
   - Pilot/POC carveout: for deals < $10k TCV, allow TFC = 1 month or no fee if they give 30-day notice (to keep pilot friction low).

3) Auto-renew: avoid unilateral auto-renew less than 60 days notice. Propose templated language that 60 days prior written notice is required to opt-out; allow discretionary shorter notice for pilot in order form appendix.

4) Operational guardrails: add explicit offboarding SLA (data export window + KV cache purge timeline) and billing prorate clause — this reduces downstream disputes.

If sales wants to be more aggressive commercially we can sign off on a 45-day notice for pilot-only or provide a one-time concession (e.g., waive TFC for the first 12 months).

I'll draft counter language and include editable sections for pilot carveouts.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Laura, David — thanks for the quick read. Sales position: agree with Laura's middle ground. Commercial ask to propose on the counter:

- 60-day standard notice, with a documented pilot appendix that allows 30–45 day notice for pilot deals under $10k TCV.
- TFC = 3 months enterprise / 1 month pilot. If Triton pushes hard on no TFC we offer a one-time waiver for the first 12 months but require written acknowledgement in the order form appendix.

We should not set precedent to accept 45 days across the board; that will create SLAs burden for capacity planning. I'll be the point for commercial concessions and will own the Mulligan (one-time waiver) if leadership OKs.

Hi Asha — thanks for sending the redline and for the patience while we routed internally. Attached is Redwood's counter (Counterproposal_Redwood_v1.docx) focusing on the items you flagged. Summary of changes we're proposing:

- Auto-renew / notice: Standard order forms will require 60 days prior written notice to opt out of auto-renew. We've added a Pilot Appendix that allows 30–45 day notice for pilot engagements under $10k TCV (we can define the exact band in the order form).
- Termination for Convenience: Enterprise order forms: capped at 3 months of average fees or documented wind-down costs, whichever is greater. Pilot order forms: 1 month TFC or fee waiver if Triton executes the written Pilot Appendix acknowledging one-time waiver terms.
- Operational clauses: added explicit offboarding timeline (30 days for data export, 90 days for cache/credentials purge) and prorated billing language during offboarding.

We're willing to include one-time commercial flexibility for Triton's initial pilot: a TFC waiver for the first 12 months if Triton signs the Pilot Appendix and confirms active usage thresholds (to avoid abuse).
